outcomes.observedOutcome: MIP import, verification, and reconstruction run headlessly from canonical package modules; no Runtime, Studio renderer, DOM, or Provider is required.
MIP documentation limits embedded digests to recomputable integrity and requires external trust or a separately specified critical signature extension for authenticity.

formatVersion is independently fixed at stable numeric 1.0.0; the published policy maps breaking core, canonical, digest, or profile changes to MAJOR, optional namespaced extensions to MINOR, and byte- and meaning-neutral clarification to PATCH.

The generic adapter module exposes contract 1.0.0, the exact five-member descriptor, definition and attestation boundary, fixed producer identity, and create, export, and artifact operations without importing a provider SDK.
Adapters consume caller-supplied settled event sequences and never start, control, retry, or claim ownership of the external Runtime.

Production CLI commands.js imports only memoryos-sdk.js; its architecture test scans every production source and rejects direct Core, MIP, Trace, Replay, Evolution, Regression, or Explorer dependencies.

Compatibility and version tables keep Standard 1.0, corrected Reference Implementation 1.2.1, Core, Adapter, SDK, CLI, report, and result 1.0.0, native artifacts 1.1, profile 1.1.0, and MIP 1.0.0 independent; the immutable initial v1.2.0 assessment remains separately identified and equality is expressly non-evidence.
The suite requires executed behavioral groups plus explicit criterion-specific review attestations; report validation rejects missing evidence, so JSON Schema alone cannot yield a semantic PASS.

Only investigation-core.js invokes native Trace, Replay, Evolution, Comparative, Regression, and Explorer implementations; Studio, SDK, and CLI consume the Core facade and contain no second execution implementation.

Explorer output contains report subjects plus digest and pointer source endpoints only; it creates no semantic payload or evidence, score, rank, summary, explanation, or causal inference and terminates at existing report digests.
CCA-MIP-1.0 is the only portable package path; native Frames remain nonportable and native export without an authored verified MIP fails instead of synthesizing package cognition.
Accepted cognition is a detached immutable observation of settled source truth; Runtime execution and state remain source-owned and are never replaced or reinterpreted by the investigation.
Each JavaScript MemoryOS owns a private in-process Core; each Python or C++ MemoryOS owns one long-lived private host with one Core, with handles confined to that client lifetime.

SDK methods forward lifecycle and artifact commands, regression operands, and Explorer report and query to the owned Core; wrappers perform ownership and shape transport checks but contain no derivation, ordering, identity, or navigation engine.
The normative change policy requires a new Standard major for removed accepted input or changed outcome, ownership, identity, ordering, lifecycle, compatibility, or passing evidence.
The normative minor-version policy preserves all prior inputs and outcomes and requires complete requirements, compatibility impact, evidence, and history for additions.

Suite 1.0.0 metadata, report schema and generator, corrected Reference Implementation 1.2.1 guide, and pinned Standard, RF, and MIP digests expose separate identities and explicitly prohibit version equality or rewriting the earlier v1.2.0 assessment as conformance evidence.
Workspace architecture publishes one headless Runtime Foundation boundary at Layer 3.
CCA-RF responsibilities are published independently; the programming model explicitly labels C++ classes, templates, and error spellings as implementation surfaces.
Required collaborations are typed dependencies supplied through RuntimeBuilder::add_provider and injected through the validated Dependency Injector graph.
Runtime, host, and component state is instance-owned; public construction and access expose no mutable global Runtime state or registry.
RuntimeState, LifecycleManager, and Runtime orchestration publish and enforce the approved normal and failure lifecycle and freeze boundary.
Typed Runtime notification is exposed and routed through the instance-local Event Bus boundary.
The programming model section 3 documents builder configuration, Configuration Manager validation, snapshot ownership, and freeze interaction.
The programming model section 7 documents logging, diagnostics, metrics, and health as Observability interactions.
The programming model has a distinct Runtime API philosophy: explicit instance ownership, typed boundaries, and immutable-after-freeze composition.

runtime-conformance-evidence.md maps CCA-RF-001 through CCA-RF-040 individually and maps ADR-003-001 through ADR-003-008 individually to concrete architecture, source, test, and documentation evidence.
cca-core/CMakeLists.txt sets the official host output name exactly to cca-runtime.
RuntimeBuilder, Runtime, and RuntimeHost use explicit object ownership; there is no public global singleton accessor.

Architecture and Runtime ownership enumerate exactly Lifecycle Manager, Service Registry, Dependency Injector, Event Bus, Configuration Manager, and Observability; surrounding host, context, and value types are explicitly non-peer surfaces.
Root architecture publishes Layers 1 through 5 exactly and names Representation, Process, and Persistence as the three Layer-4 Domain Engines.
Architecture fixes dependencies higher-to-lower; Runtime target dependencies are confined to lower-layer core and platform facilities with no compiler or Domain Engine dependency.
The complete public Service Registry resolution interface is template- and contract-typed and exposes no string service identifier lookup.
Public resolution exposes Service Contract interfaces; Provider records, factories, concrete identities, and instances remain private to Runtime composition.
Every ServiceContract instantiation requires an explicit compile-time ServiceCardinality argument.
EventBus::publish<Event> is the typed asynchronous notification boundary and returns a shared future; delivery is not inline.
StartupExecutionPolicy permits parallel_within_level while retaining sequential as an option; each level is joined before the next.
The programming model section 4 is a distinct service contract, provider, cardinality, and registration section.
The programming model section 5 is a distinct dependency declaration and constructor-injection section.
The programming model section 7 is a distinct RuntimeResult, diagnostic, failure, and rollback error-reporting section.
The programming model section 9 specifies thread-safety and lifetime constraints for host, Runtime, all six components, contracts, Providers, handlers, and immutable snapshots.
